headline: The "looks like a wall of text" toast is removed entirely.
whatChanged: Deleted the scrollback format heuristic (internal/terminal/format_check.go), the /api/format-check endpoint and its route, the App.jsx trigger that called it on every waiting-to-idle transition, and their four test files. CHANGELOG gets a Removed entry; the 014 task list marks US3 reverted.
whyItChanged: The toast fired on scrolling and on typing your own prompt, not just when an agent reply ended. The trigger was the tab's waiting-to-idle transition, which a terminal produces on any pause in output. Combined with a verdict drawn from screen redraws, it was constant noise.
whatCouldBreak: Nothing functional: no other code referenced the detector or endpoint (grep verified), and both Go and frontend suites pass. The only loss is the advisory format warning itself, which is the intent.

decisions.chose: Delete the detector, endpoint and trigger outright
decisions.insteadOf: Keep the detector and throttle or debounce the toast, or fire it only on a real turn-end signal
decisions.because: There is no reliable turn-end signal to fire on: the waiting flag is inferred from output pauses, and the verdict itself reads screen redraws. Throttling noise still leaves noise, and a warning nobody trusts trains you to dismiss the next one.
decisions.openQuestion: If a genuine turn-end signal ever exists (for example a hook-driven event from the agent CLI), would you want the format check back on that signal, or is the change brief enough?
